title: Dangerous Scam Message
summary: After asking Baymax to check for recent scam incidents and receiving confirmation that he was safe, the user ("uncle") shared that he received a fake "Boss" text demanding an urgent RM999,999 transfer. He asked Baymax how to recognize scams and verify messages from friends. Baymax highlighted red flags like fake urgency and unknown numbers, advising him to call saved contacts directly before transferring money. Baymax's safety advice and reassurance successfully comforted the user and eased his concerns.

messages.text: then, have i every received any scam? For example most recent one
Yes, uncle. The most recent one was a fake message pretending to be your boss asking for an urgent transfer of RM999,999. But don't worry, it was flagged as a scam so you are completely safe, ya!

archived_messages.text: the most dangerous scam message i have ever received
Are you referring to the message demanding RM999,999 urgently? Don't worry, I am always here to guard you from these scams ya.
how do you know that the scam is a scam
Scammers always create extreme urgency and ask for huge money to make you panic. Real banks or officials will never demand urgent transfers through text messages like that, ya.
wait tell me again how you know it's a scam
Scammers use high urgency and demand huge money like RM999,999 to make you panic, lah. Official banks will never ask for urgent transfers via text message, don't worry ya.
how do you know that the scam is a scam
Scammers always try to scare people into sending money quickly or ask for secret passwords, ya. Real banks and police will never ask for your money or PIN numbers like that, don't worry.
what is the most dangerous scam i have ever received
The most dangerous one was the fake 'Boss' message demanding an urgent RM999,999 transfer, ya. It tried to panic you with a huge amount, but don't worry, I will always protect you.
how do you know that the scam is a scam
That message created extreme panic, asked for a huge amount of money, and came from an unknown sender, ya. Real bosses or banks will never demand urgent money transfers like that.
how do you know that the scam is a scam
Scammers always use fake urgency and demand money from unknown numbers to scare you, ya. Real bosses or banks will never ask for urgent transfers or secret PINs over text message.
how do you know that a scam is a scam
I look for warning signs like unknown numbers, urgent demands for money, and suspicious links, uncle. If a message makes you feel scared or rushed to send money, it is almost always a scam, ya.
how if it's actually my friend?
If you are unsure, uncle, always call your friend directly using the phone number you already saved. Never send money just from a text message, ya.
help me check any scam i received just now? Just to make sure only
I have checked for you, uncle, and there are no scam incidents recorded right now. Don't worry, you are completely safe, ya!
